transcript.sourceText: Without trade, price is $50 and quantity is 30. At the $30 world price, domestic production is 10 and consumption is 50, so imports are 40. Each gain-from-trade triangle has height $50 - $30 = $20. The production-side base is 30 - 10 = 20; the consumption-side base is 50 - 30 = 20. Total gains are 2 × (1/2 × 20 × 20) = $400.
transcript.text: Without trade, price is dollars 50 and quantity is 30. At the dollars 30 world price, domestic production is 10 and consumption is 50, so imports are 40. Each gain-from-trade triangle has height dollars 50 minus dollars 30 equals dollars 20 . The production-side base is 30 minus 10 equals 20 ; the consumption-side base is 50 minus 30 equals 20 . Total gains are 2 times (1 divided by 2 times 20 times 20) equals dollars 400 .

MICROECONOMICS
MICRO-17
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Calculate Gains from Trade, Surplus & Winners/Losers.
Difficulty: Advanced
THE CORE IDEA

International trade changes consumer and producer surplus and creates net gains when the world price differs from the no-trade equilibrium price. The surplus framework converts distributional changes into a net total-surplus comparison. Trade creates net gains while redistributing surplus between buyers and sellers.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
Trade creates net gains while redistributing surplus between buyers and sellers.
The efficiency result is based on the net change in combined surplus, not on every group winning.
Higher export prices redistribute surplus toward producers while creating a positive net gain in the standard model.
Aggregate gains do not imply universal gains.
WATCH OUT

Do not assume trade has only winners or only losers. Trade creates net gains while redistributing surplus between buyers and sellers. The efficiency result is based on the net change in combined surplus, not on every group winning.
WORKED EXAMPLE: TRACING TRADE WINNERS AND LOSERS

Without trade, price is $50 and quantity is 30. At the $30 world price, domestic production is 10 and consumption is 50, so imports are 40. Each gain-from-trade triangle has height $50 - $30 = $20. The production-side base is 30 - 10 = 20; the consumption-side base is 50 - 30 = 20. Total gains are 2 × (1/2 × 20 × 20) = $400.
